# EnterpriseGlue v0.27.3 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.27.2`.

## Highlights

- **database-migration-runtime:** Separates database migration configuration from application authentication and encryption secrets for least-privilege deployment jobs.
- **release-and-database-upgrade:** Regenerates the signed schema-epoch executable digest after the migration configuration boundary changed an inventoried source file.

## User and administrator impact

- Database migration and readiness jobs can start with only their database-scoped configuration and credentials.
- Release candidates can verify and publish the database-only migration runtime without weakening the signed schema-epoch bridge.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Redeploy the matching host chart and backend image so database jobs use the database-only configuration boundary.
- Use the matching host package, backend image, and Helm chart so every copy contains the same regenerated schema-epoch manifest.

## Configuration

- No new environment variables are required; existing database, tenancy, schema-epoch, and adapter settings retain their names and defaults.
- Migration and preflight jobs must continue to mount their dedicated database Secrets and must not receive JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, or ENCRYPTION_KEY.
- No configuration changes are required; migration and preflight jobs continue to use only their database-scoped configuration and credentials.

## Database migrations

- No schema migration is added and the PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and Spanner TypeORM adapter contracts are unchanged.
- Pooled-tenancy, owner migration, schema-epoch preflight, RLS, and runtime-grant behavior remain enabled through database-scoped configuration.
- The executable migration ceiling, accepted ledger digests, PostgreSQL policy profiles, and all five TypeORM adapter behaviors are unchanged.
- Only the source-content digest of the existing 16-file owner-transition implementation inventory changes.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Application authentication, administrator, and encryption secrets are no longer prerequisites of the migration module graph or inputs to database migration and preflight jobs.
- The application runtime retains full production validation of JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, and ENCRYPTION_KEY.
- The regenerated digest binds the database-only configuration import and deferred application-only seeding dependency introduced by the migration configuration boundary.
- The manifest update command deterministically updates the canonical package copy and byte-identical Helm chart copy together.

## Documentation

- The host chart operator documentation describes the database-only configuration boundary for migration and preflight jobs.
- The schema-epoch architecture documentation records the deterministic manifest write and verification workflow.

## Known limitations

- Database credentials remain adapter-specific and must still be scoped separately for owner migration, preflight, and application runtime identities.
- Changing any of the 16 inventoried executable sources requires running the manifest write workflow and reviewing the resulting digest before candidate publication.

## Rollback

- Redeploy the prior matching backend image and host chart; no database rollback or data restoration is required.
- Revert this change together with the migration configuration boundary; do not combine the previous manifest digest with the updated migration runtime bytes.

## Validation evidence

- Focused configuration and module-boundary tests prove production migration imports succeed without application secrets.
- Negative configuration tests prove every supported adapter still rejects missing required connection fields and PostgreSQL still rejects the public application schema.
- TypeORM adapter, migration orchestration, Helm rendering, PostgreSQL integration, and database portability gates cover the unchanged database behavior.
- Manifest generation tests prove deterministic output, canonical/chart byte identity, source-mutation sensitivity, and verification against the regenerated digest.
- The focused database-portability gate now verifies schema-epoch manifest integrity, and deterministic path classification sends manifest and generator changes through database qualification before release staging.
- Focused schema-epoch, release-receipt, package, migration-boundary, and five-adapter tests preserve the existing runtime contract.
